## How the PLAYER MCP gateway answers

As anyone who calls or runs the gateway
I want one shape for its answers and its refusals to start
so that a client and a deployment can rely on it without reading the code.

**Rule: A configuration the deployment contract forbids stops the gateway before it listens.**

## Log in to the PLAYER MCP gateway

As the MCP client of a player (Claude.ai, an agent's MCP connector)
I want to find where to log in and be let in only with a valid WorkOS token
so that a player's world answers only to that player.

The gateway is an OAuth protected resource (RFC 9728): it checks AuthKit
access tokens against the issuer's published keys and runs no
authorization server of its own.

Status: **verified** · Code: [`createPlayerJwtVerifier`](../../spellkave-gateway-identity/src/resource-server.ts)

> AuthKit rotates keys; a token with a key id the gateway has not seen yet makes it fetch the issuer's keys once more instead of refusing.

## Start playing through the MCP tools

As a player who logged in through an MCP client
I want to see the PLAYER tools, read the modding docs and be told where to
claim a hero
so that my client can start without knowing the world first.

Every scenario here runs without a hero: a hero lives in a live world the
gateway reaches over a SpacetimeDB subscription, which this offline suite
does not have. What a player with a hero sees is proved by the live suites
(`authority-tools.live.test.ts`, `parameterized-scenes.live.test.ts`).

## Call the gateway from a browser

As a browser page (claude.ai, the spellkave.com website, a map editor)
I want my allowed origin to get CORS answers, and anything else refused
so that a player's token works only from pages the player trusts.

The default origin allowlist is the canonical host, claude.ai and the
website (spellkave.com, www.spellkave.com, localhost). A deployment that
sets SPELLKAVE_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGIN_HOSTNAMES replaces it; the canonical host
and the website hosts stay in the list either way. Map tiles and the OSM API
under /w/<slug> answer any origin, because map editors run anywhere; they
still need a login.

### An allowed origin's preflight is answered without a token

Status: **verified** · Code: [`withMcpCors`](../src/mcp-cors.ts)

> A browser sends the preflight without credentials, so it must not need one. The default allowlist is the canonical host, claude.ai, spellkave.com, www.spellkave.com and localhost.

- Given the gateway runs

## Run and watch the gateway

As the operator of a Spellkave deployment
I want the gateway to start from its configuration, report honest health
and log every request without secrets
so that I can roll it, probe it and debug it without reading tokens.

### The gateway is unavailable while the issuer is down

Status: **verified** · Code: [`createIssuerReadiness`](../src/runtime.ts)

- Given the gateway runs
- Given the issuer is down
- When I send "GET /healthz"

  ```console
  $ curl -q -s -i -X GET $MCP/healthz
  HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  content-type: application/json
  x-request-id: 59aeb3e6-73b5-4a79-b5ee-4236d6a2151b
  Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 22:10:27 GMT
  Connection: keep-alive
  Keep-Alive: timeout=5
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  {"service":"spellkave-player-mcp","status":"unavailable"}
  [exit 0]
  ```

- Then the answer is 503
- Then the JSON answer is:
- When I run the health check

  ```console
  $ spellkave-player-mcp-health
  [exit 1]
  ```

- Then the health check exits with 1

### The gateway starts from its front door and stops on SIGTERM

Status: **verified** · Code: [`spellkave-player-mcp.js`](../bin/spellkave-player-mcp.js)

> The container runs bin/spellkave-player-mcp; its health check runs bin/spellkave-player-mcp-health against the same environment.
